page: Amazon Web Services m7i-flex.8xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8488C processor with an x86_64 architecture, providing 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 3.2 GHz and includes a 105 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2023.0 and high throughput in single-threaded gzip compression at 32.42 GB/sec. The processor supports advanced instruction sets, including Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512, which assist in cryptographic and vector operations. Multi-core performance is solid, as shown by a Passmark CPU score of 47332.26 and a stress-ng multi-core metric of 32413.77. In memory-bound tasks, the DDR5 memory achieves a read-only cached small block bandwidth of 2436.4 GB/sec and an uncached large block read bandwidth of 170.39 GB/sec.

The m7i-flex.8xlarge offers a cost-efficient profile for general-purpose workloads by utilizing a resource-dense architecture that balances compute and memory without the added cost of bundled local storage. However, workloads requiring high-speed local scratch space will face tradeoffs due to the lack of local NVMe drives. While the instance performs well in text processing, image processing, and static web serving, it exhibits limitations in heavy AI workloads. For example, large language model inference text generation using a 70B model is weak, averaging only 2.67 tokens/sec. This instance is best suited for application servers, web serving, software compilation, database operations, and moderate-scale serialization tasks.
